summary: Round-3 verification of the three round-2 items on M5.40's split. All three hold. (1) TABLE WHOLE: header `| ID | Task | Serves | State |` is line 25 and every line from 26 to the end of the table is pipe-prefixed -- no blank line survives inside it; rows read M5.39 (53), M5.40 (54), M5.40a (55), M5.40b (56), M5.41 (57). (2) BOTH NUMBERS CORRECT: 12,800 MiB / 1024 = 12.5 GiB exactly; 1,600 / 0.001 = 1.6e6 = six orders; charging only the cross-AZ share, (2/3)(1.6e6) = 1.07e6, still six. No `12.8 GiB`, no 'five orders' and no `%%` anywhere in the file. The PREMISE was checked against the code rather than the prose: SubscriptionHub.publishSegment builds one Target per (subscription, run) (SubscriptionHub.java:345-354) and deliver() opens one sink per Target then calls source.writeTo(all sinks) ONCE, so every sink receives the WHOLE segment -- 1,600 targets x 8 MiB is what the code does. (3) CRITERION-6 PREMISE CORRECT: M5/SPEC.md:342-343 reads 'holds service memory flat in K, at K = 1 and K = 64, with a bound independent of K'. M5.40b now restates it as flat-in-K with a K-independent bound, which is what makes the 'a cache of capacity C adds C at every K' argument follow, and it names thePeakHandOffAndTheReadCountAreIDENTICALAtKONEAndKSIXTYFOUR (SegmentProxyTest.java:270) as one test OF the criterion; that test's own javadoc does say 'It is not evidence for criterion 6 on its own', as cited. CITATIONS CHECKED AGAINST THE TREE: M5.45a resolves (backlog.md:62) and is committed (d944a24); AssembledServingPathTest.aSegmentOfMANYRunsIsReadONCENotOncePerRun exists (AssembledServingPathTest.java:202), so M5.40's 'a test does see it' is true of the tree and not only of the row. COST LENS: the closing claim is that the caller-granularity half is closed -- one streamTo per segment, GET count 1 -- and the code shows exactly one serving call for all targets. Nothing here adds an object-store request that scales with runs, shards or indices; what scales with runs is PUSH BYTES, which is where M5.40a now files it. Recommend landing.

findings.what: `Doc 10 s4's` where every other section reference in the file uses the section sign: lines 41, 53, 54, 60, 79, 98-101, 254, 257, 266 all read `§<n>`. Line 56 is the only `s<n>` in the file -- the same class of leftover as the `%%` already fixed.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader grepping backlog.md for `§4` to find every row that leans on doc 10 section 4 misses M5.40b, which is the row whose whole cost argument rests on doc 10 §4's 'AZ recovery: many nodes replaying the same backlog'. One character.

findings.what: The row pins its severity to NFR-5's ABSOLUTE target (< 0.1% of ingested bytes, requirements.md:34), but that target is not reachable by the FIX either: one stream per CONSUMER still pushes the whole 8 MiB to each of ~9 nodes, ~6x ingested bytes crossing an AZ, three orders over 0.1%. The property a taker can actually write a criterion against is PROPORTIONALITY -- pushed bytes scale with consumers per segment, never with runs per segment.
findings.failure_scenario: This is the mirror of the round-2 finding the row was split to answer. There the risk was a criterion written against a number that is already correct (NFR-4's GET count); here it is a criterion written against a number nothing can reach, so a taker who writes 'cross-AZ bytes < 0.1% of ingested' as M5.40a's acceptance criterion cannot close the row even after implementing exactly the contract change the row asks for, and discovers that only after doing the work.
